audit_findings.title: Positive growth applied to a negative anchor reverses the scenario logic
audit_findings.magnitude: BASE and BULL equity values are $163 million and $216 million below BEAR, respectively, equivalent to $1.99 and $2.63 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: Growth compounds the negative $32.4 million OE anchor, enlarging losses and producing increasingly negative operating and terminal values
audit_findings.evidence: Our net income declined 35.2% to $17.4 million, or $0.21 per diluted share, in 2025 from $26.9 million, or $0.33 per diluted share, in 2024.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated modeling error: the stated bull case produces the lowest value because positive growth expands a loss. The resulting scenario values cannot represent bear, base and recovery outcomes and are capable of changing the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Replace percentage growth on the negative anchor with explicit loss-to-breakeven and normalized positive-OE paths, then rerun all scenarios and the margin-of-safety threshold; otherwise report only the too-hard conclusion.

audit_findings.title: The null perimeter ignores the Intermodal disposal
audit_findings.magnitude: 2025 Intermodal revenue was $33.671 million and operating loss was $1.883 million; total continuing-operations OE effect is unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: The disposed segment remains in historical earnings, capital expenditure and working-capital movements while the June 2026 cash bridge reflects the post-sale company
audit_findings.evidence: Our Intermodal operations were sold effective September 30, 2025.
audit_findings.explanation: The perimeter mismatch is demonstrated. Removing the $1.883 million operating loss would improve earnings, but removing Intermodal capital expenditure, working capital and disposal effects could move OE in either direction. The segment's scale and the negative $32.4 million anchor make a continuing-operations rerun necessary.
audit_findings.action: Reconstruct 2025 and relevant historical OE on a continuing-operations basis, separately removing Intermodal operating results, depreciation, capital expenditure, working capital and disposal cash flows, then rerun the anchor and scenarios.

audit_findings.title: Intermodal sale proceeds may contaminate owner earnings through net capital expenditure
audit_findings.magnitude: Potential $51.8 million OE overstatement, equal to 160% of the absolute $32.4 million anchor, before DCF amplification
audit_findings.mechanism: Including the strategic asset-sale proceeds in net capital expenditure raises OE; adding sale-derived cash again through the cash bridge would count the same value twice
audit_findings.evidence: The transaction was structured as an asset sale of certain Intermodal equipment, including over 1,200 refrigerated containers, and associated customer contracts to Hub Group, Inc. for $51.8 million in cash.
audit_findings.explanation: The $51.8 million sale is filed, but the supplied record does not establish whether it entered the OE ledger. If it did, the amount is plainly material relative to the anchor and would make the current value too high despite the reported negative valuation.
audit_findings.action: Trace the $101.676 million of 2025 revenue-equipment disposition proceeds in the OE ledger, identify the $51.8 million strategic sale separately, exclude it from recurring net capital expenditure, and rerun OE and the bridge with the proceeds recognized only once.

audit_findings.title: Latest-year capital expenditure may not represent maintenance requirements
audit_findings.magnitude: FY2025 revenue-equipment additions net of disposition proceeds were $39.955 million, versus approximately $109 million of projected net capital expenditure for the remainder of 2026; normalized maintenance capital is unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: The maintenance-capital charge directly reduces OE and therefore affects the negative anchor, every forecast year and terminal value
audit_findings.evidence: We estimate that capital expenditures, net of proceeds from dispositions, will be approximately $92 million in 2026.
audit_findings.explanation: The filed capital program shows substantial timing variability, while the model capitalizes one negative latest-year OE figure indefinitely. The record does not establish whether the charge is inflated by replacement timing or understated by fleet contraction and unusually high disposition proceeds, but the observed scale is sufficient to affect the conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Calculate normalized maintenance capital from continuing fleet counts, replacement ages, unit costs and ordinary disposal proceeds; separate growth, contraction and divestiture spending, then rerun the OE history and valuation.

audit_findings.title: Self-insurance estimates could leave an unrecognized claim ahead of common equity
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified; $43.443 million was accrued at June 30, 2026, and the current policy has a $5.0 million per-claim auto-liability retention plus specified $5.0 million aggregate layers
audit_findings.mechanism: Adverse claim development would reduce future OE or create an additional liability ahead of common equity
audit_findings.evidence: Projection of losses is subject to a high level of estimation uncertainty and actual results could differ from these current estimates.
audit_findings.explanation: No unrecorded claim or inadequate reserve is demonstrated. Claims expense is already retained in OE, the latest reserve was $43.443 million, and an automatic additional deduction would double count recorded estimates. The increased retention and uncertain litigation outcomes remain forward-looking exposures requiring monitoring.
audit_findings.action: Review subsequent reserve development, actuarial ranges, large open claims and litigation disclosures; rerun OE or the bridge only for a filed reserve increase or a supportable probable loss not already accrued.

audit_findings.title: Restricted Intermodal escrow may have been included as excess cash
audit_findings.magnitude: $0 valuation impact: the $103.98 million bridge equals reported cash and cash equivalents and excludes the separately reported $5.0 million escrow; the escrow would otherwise equal about $0.06 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: A restricted escrow would overstate the cash bridge only if included as distributable cash
audit_findings.evidence: These funds are restricted from use for general corporate purposes.
audit_findings.explanation: The latest balance sheet reports $103.980 million of cash and cash equivalents plus a separate $5.0 million escrow. The valuation bridge uses exactly $103.98 million, demonstrating that the restricted amount was excluded. Consequently, this finding does not affect the current valuation.
audit_findings.action: Retain the balance-sheet trace showing the escrow exclusion and reassess only after its December 2026 release or if an indemnity claim changes the recoverable amount.
